what_the_eye_sees: A plain polished half-round band with a small orange stone in a round bezel. Patches of granulation are scattered on the shoulders and flanks. The beads all look the same size and height, and they sit in blocky vertical clusters with bald, mirror-smooth metal between them. At 300 px it reads as granulation work, a sea-urchin or blackberry texture, or a 'bubbles' band. It does not read as reptile hide. Most of the surface is bare metal and the beads look applied on top, so a jeweller would say 'granulated band with a citrine' and would not name a Gila monster or any lizard. No dorsal bead row can be seen along the crest, and nothing belly-like shows. The two-height reticulated banding that should carry the animal is not visible.
changes: Bead the whole shoulder and flank surface (theta 35 to 145 and 215 to 325, crest to edge fillet) with no bald metal. Close the smooth gaps completely so that bare land between beads is only the 0.42 x pitch lattice land. Acceptance: in face-300 and hero-300 no smooth patch wider than about 2 bead pitches remains outside the stone mound.

Carry the Gila banding with height and not with bead presence. Put high beads (0.36 mm) in forking, irregular reticulated transverse bands about 3 to 5 beads wide, and low, flatter beads (0.24 mm, cushion remap) in the bands between. Replace the current rectangular vertical blocks with the organic forked mask. Acceptance: at 300 px you can see alternating dark-shadowed high-bead bands and lower, brighter bead fields that branch and merge, and the edges are not rectilinear.

Put in a clear dorsal bead row along the crest (about 1.1 mm domes, 0.42 mm high, tapering in size away from 90 degrees) that runs into the spessartite as its central bead, and grade the beads from flattened shingles at the crest to full domes at the edges. Acceptance: in face-300 a single continuous bead line runs along the crest through the stone, and the bead size visibly changes from crest to edge.
